kpi_specs.name: Total Revenue
kpi_specs.description: The sum of all invoice totals, representing the overall revenue generated.
kpi_specs.sql_query: SELECT SUM("Total") AS total_revenue FROM data
kpi_specs.reasoning: Total revenue is a fundamental KPI for any retail or e-commerce business. It provides a single summary metric of overall performance, making it ideal for a card visualization.

kpi_specs.name: Revenue by Country
kpi_specs.description: Total revenue grouped by billing country, identifying top revenue-generating markets.
kpi_specs.sql_query: SELECT "BillingCountry", SUM("Total") AS revenue FROM data GROUP BY "BillingCountry" ORDER BY revenue DESC
kpi_specs.reasoning: Revenue by country is a standard retail KPI for understanding geographic performance. The BillingCountry column has low cardinality (24 distinct values), making it well-suited for a bar chart comparison.

kpi_specs.name: Monthly Revenue Trend
kpi_specs.description: Total revenue aggregated by month to show trends over time.
kpi_specs.sql_query: SELECT strftime('%Y-%m', "InvoiceDate") AS month, SUM("Total") AS revenue FROM data GROUP BY month ORDER BY month
kpi_specs.reasoning: Tracking revenue over time is critical for identifying trends and seasonality. The InvoiceDate column allows for monthly aggregation, which is ideal for a line chart showing temporal patterns.

kpi_specs.name: Average Invoice Value by Customer
kpi_specs.description: Average invoice total per customer, highlighting high-value customers.
kpi_specs.sql_query: SELECT "CustomerId", AVG("Total") AS avg_invoice_value FROM data GROUP BY "CustomerId" ORDER BY avg_invoice_value DESC
kpi_specs.reasoning: Average invoice value by customer helps identify high-value customers and segments. The CustomerId column has moderate cardinality (59 distinct values), making it suitable for a bar chart comparison.

kpi_specs.name: Top 10 Customers by Revenue
kpi_specs.description: Ranking of customers by total revenue generated, identifying the most valuable customers.
kpi_specs.sql_query: SELECT "CustomerId", SUM("Total") AS total_revenue FROM data GROUP BY "CustomerId" ORDER BY total_revenue DESC LIMIT 10
kpi_specs.reasoning: Identifying top customers by revenue is essential for customer relationship management. A table is appropriate here to display the ranked list with exact revenue values for clarity.
